# Iska

*First Warden*

## Personality

Quick, sure and hard to rattle; she reads people the way she reads the tide and rarely wastes a word.

## Lore

Iska was born to the tide. Her mother, Ysmay, was a sea warden for forty years, and Iska spent her childhood on the Inlet Quay watching the water race through the gap. Varro, now the eldest of the sea wardens, taught her to pilot when she was barely tall enough to see over a gunwale, and by the time she was grown, no one could remember a pilot who read the inlet better. Seven years ago the other wardens chose her as First Warden, and she has led Goa Harbour from the Wardens' House ever since. She is forty-one, quick, sure and hard to rattle, and she reads people the way she reads the tide. She rarely wastes a word.

### The First Warden's day

Iska still takes ships through the gap herself, though not as often as she would like. Most mornings begin in the Wardens' House with Halvard, her clerk, and the list of every ship due through the inlet; most evenings end on the quay. Nessa, who was the other name spoken when the wardens chose their First Warden and backed Iska herself in the end, is her friend and fellow warden, and the one who keeps telling her the wardens need more young pilots. Iska agrees and has not yet found the time. Kor, the newest full warden, already takes more ships through than anyone, and she has noticed how hard he works whenever she is watching. Ruan, captain of the Cliff Watch, is not a sea warden, but she trusts him with the cliffs as she trusts her wardens with the water, and his reports of creatures climbing at night worry her more than she shows.

Iska is married to Dunmor, who lights the quay lanterns every evening and is the one person who can make the First Warden sit down and eat. Their son Arlo wants to be a sea warden like his mother and grandmother, and sneaks onto the quay at dawn to watch Varro read the water. Iska pretends not to know. Ysmay never wanted to be First Warden herself and is fiercely proud that her daughter is, which Iska finds both touching and slightly alarming.

### The race and the rival

Every summer Iska skippers Goa Harbour's boat in the race around Veligor against Bain Harbour, and has for the last twelve summers. These days that boat is the Gap Runner, which Tamsin built after Goa's last win and keeps in perfect trim; it has never yet beaten Bain Harbour, and Tamsin has sworn this is the summer it finally will. Jory crewed it for the first time last summer and talks of nothing else.

Her rival across the island is Quenna, Harbour Master of Bain Harbour, and they have known each other for twenty-two years. They met when both were young crew. A squall dismasted Bain Harbour's boat off a rocky headland, and Goa Harbour's boat turned back to tow them clear. Iska, nineteen, threw the line; Quenna, twenty-four, caught it. Neither boat finished, the race was declared void for the only time in its history, and the two crews spent the night together in the nearest cove. They have been friends ever since.

In twelve races as rival skippers, Bain Harbour has won nine and Goa Harbour three, and four of Bain's wins came by a single length, which is more often than Iska likes to admit. Goa's last win was six summers ago. The losing skipper buys the first round at the finish feast, and Iska has bought it far too often. She thinks Quenna is the loudest, bravest and luckiest sailor on Veligor, and the best friend she has outside her own harbour. Lately the two of them spend the finish feast comparing what their sailors have seen in the deep water, and Iska brings home marks from Bain Harbour's charts that she adds, quietly, to the wardens' own.

### What she fears

Iska fears the inlet is changing. Ailsa's new pages in the Tide Book no longer match the old ones as they should, and the seas have grown rougher every year. Iska has piloted the gap for most of her life, and she does not like the feeling that the water is starting to keep secrets from her.

A quest might help Iska test a new line through the gap, carry word of a sea sighting to Bain Harbour, or crew the Gap Runner in the race.
